concepts.def: Induced EMF = -d(flux)/dt; magnitude proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux (Faraday 1831).
Direction of induced current opposes the change producing it; conserves energy (Lenz 1834).

Induced loops in solid conductors dissipate energy; laminated cores reduce them.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Electromagnetic Induction — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Electromagnetic Induction brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Electromagnetic Induction.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
